text:
I wrote `src/app/app.ts`, `src/app/main.ts` and `public/index.html`. Typecheck and drift are both clean, but I haven't run the app, so the routes and the page are untested.

- **App:** `createApp()` takes no parameter, because the design has no database node. `ItemStore` still needs a `DatabaseSync`, so `createApp` makes its own in-memory one. Routes:
  - `POST /api/users`
  - `POST /api/items`
  - `GET /api/items`
  - `GET /api/items/:id`, with an optional `?displayCurrency=`
  - `POST /api/items/:id/bids`
  - `/health`, registered first
- **Currency conversion:** `ItemController.getItem` returns null for the converted prices. The route handler fills them in using `ExchangeRateService`.
- **Circular dependency:** `EventFeed` and `EventSubscriber` each take the other in their constructors. I created the subscriber with a placeholder feed, so the subscriber never receives the real feed. The feed delivers into a subscriber that only stores events. Nothing reaches `LiveGateway`, so there are no live WebSocket updates. The page refreshes the open item every 3 seconds instead.
- **Frankfurter and the closer:** the real `FrankfurterApi` is a small fetch-based object in `app.ts`. `main.ts` starts the auction-closing timer, since `AuctionCloser`'s own start method is private.
- **Fix in `ItemStore`:** it queried status `'Open'`, but the enum value is `'open'`, so no open items would ever have been found. It now uses `'open'`.

One bug I left alone: `ItemService.closeDueAuctions` always sets the status to `closed`, even when there was no bid. Items with no bids are never marked `unsold`.
